title: Stocks Mostly Down Pre-Bell as Investors Await Data on Wholesale Prices, Retail Sales
detail:
PREMIUM
Stocks Mostly Down Pre-Bell as Investors Await Data on Wholesale Prices, Retail Sales
MT Newswires
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 4:27 AM PDT 3 min read
^GSPC
^NDX
^DJI
^IXIC
stock trading floor NYSE market wall street -Shutterstock

US equity markets were mostly pointing lower before the opening bell Thursday as traders await key data on wholesale prices and retail sales.

The S&P 500 declined 0.3% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.1% in premarket activity, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.3%. Wall Street closed Wednesday trading in the red, with the Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 down for the third consecutive session.

September's producer price index, a measure of wholesale prices, is scheduled to be released at 8:30 am ET. Official data is expected to show that producer prices rose 0.6% and 5.4% last month on sequential and annual bases, respectively, according to a Bloomberg-compiled consensus.

The retail sales report for September is also out at 8:30 am. Sales are expected to rise 0.3% last month after climbing 1.2% in August.

The two reports come after government data showed Wednesday that last month's annual consumer price growth reached the highest level since May, boosting bets on a second straight Federal Reserve rate hike later in October.

"The larger than expected increase in the core CPI in September increases the odds that the (Fed) raises rates at its meeting later this month," Oxford Economics Lead US Economist Nancy Vanden Houten said in remarks emailed to MT Newswires on Wednesday.

Markets are currently pricing in a 71% probability that the central bank will keep its benchmark rate steady later this month, with the remaining odds in favor of a 25-basis-point hike, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Treasury yields dropped early Thursday, with the two-year rate retreating 7 basis points to 4.73% and the 10-year rate plunging 11 basis points to 5.08%.

Thursday's economic calendar also has the weekly jobless claims bulletin followed by the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index and the Empire State manufacturing index, both for this month.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is slated to speak at 11:30 pm, while Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack speaks earlier at 4:30 pm.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil dipped 0.4% to $94.73 a barrel, while Brent fell 1.9% to $104.09.

The US is considering easing sanctions on some of Russia's unregulated shadow fleet tankers to help lower freight rates and increase flexibility in diesel shipments, Reuters reported Wednesday, citing an official.

Two Singapore-registered container vessels were reportedly struck by unknown projectiles while transiting the Strait of Hormuz earlier this week, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore said in a statement.

The chief of Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps said Wednesday that Tehran is "counting the moments" until it can sink US warships, CNBC reported, citing state-affiliated media.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing's (TSM) US-listed stock declined nearly 2% pre-bell after the chipmaker issued a fourth-quarter gross margin outlook that implied a sequential decrease at the midpoint.

Charles Schwab (SCHW), Prologis (PLD), Bank of New York Mellon (BNY), US Bancorp (USB), PNC Financial Services (PNC), First Horizon (FHN) and Commercial Metals (CMC) report their latest financial results before the bell, among others.

J.B. Hunt Transport Services (JBHT) posts its earnings after the markets close.

Spot gold increased 1.7% to $4,176 per troy ounce, while bitcoin traded down 0.8% at $81,073.

Investing.com - Futures linked to Canada's main stock index pointed slightly higher on Thursday, suggesting a rebound from a fall in the prior session, as investors assessed jitters around the artificial intelligence trade and elevated Federal Reserve interest rates.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

By 06:01 ET (10:01 GMT), the S&P/TSX 60 index standard futures contract had risen by 3 points, or 0.2%. On Wednesday, the S&P/TSX composite index slid by 1.11% to 35,584.46, retreating from a three-week high.

Materials stocks, which include metal mining shares, were among the biggest laggards, while the financial and technology sectors also dipped.

S&P, Nasdaq futures fall

S&P and Nasdaq futures dropped. By 06:11 ET, the S&P futures contract had dropped by 22 points, or 0.3%, and Nasdaq 100 futures had declined by 326 points, or 1.1%. Dow futures, on the other hand, edged up by 147 points, or 0.3%.

The main averages on Wall Street all fell on Wednesday. A hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report sparked a temporary rush to increase bets on a Federal Reserve interest rate hike later this month, pushing up U.S. Treasury yields in the process.

Those wagers later moderated. Investors are now expecting 30 basis points of Fed rate hikes over the rest of the year, compared to 25 basis points previously, while expectations for about 50 basis points of increases in 2027 held roughly steady analysts at Vital Knowledge said in a note.

Treasuries rebounded as well, with yields ending the day flat-to-down and last trading lower. Yields tend to move inversely to bond prices.

Partially driving the recovery in debt markets were fresh concerns over AI, specifically how higher-for-longer rates could impact a capital-intensive sector supported by debt-fueled fundraising and grappling with intensifying competition at home and abroad.

"Markets have just had an incredibly tumultuous 24 hours, as a strong US CPI print was then followed up with mounting fears around the AI trade," analysts at Deutsche Bank said in a note.

"[I]t just shows how much AI is dominating market attention right now, as fears over a broader tightening in credit conditions led to growing doubts about whether the Fed would actually move, despite the strong print."

CoreWeave has been among the hardest hit by the downturn in AI stocks. The neocloud player slid by more than 6% in premarket U.S. trading, after having fallen by over 15% a day earlier. Some of the company's bonds tumbled to new lows in secondary markets.

US Stock Futures Fall as AI Valuation Concerns Offset Anthropic Revenue Growth and TSMC Record Profit: Dow Jones, S&P, Nasdaq, Wall Street

Trading disclosure

US stock futures moved lower on Thursday as concerns about artificial intelligence valuations, corporate borrowing and the prospect of higher interest rates continued to weigh on investor sentiment, despite reports of strong revenue growth at Anthropic and record quarterly earnings from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company.

At 02:54 ET (06:54 GMT), Dow Jones futures were up 27 points, or 0.1%, while S&P 500 futures declined 38 points, or 0.5%. Nasdaq 100 futures fell 407 points, or 1.4%, indicating continued pressure on technology stocks ahead of the opening bell.

The weakness followed a sharp decline on Wall Street during the previous session, when stronger-than-expected US inflation data prompted investors to reassess the outlook for Federal Reserve interest rates.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite recorded their largest single-session declines since July, with AI-related companies particularly affected.

AI Investment Concerns Weigh on Technology Stocks

Wednesday's market sell-off followed the release of US consumer price data showing a larger-than-anticipated increase in September inflation.

The figures prompted investors to increase expectations of a possible Federal Reserve interest rate rise at its meeting later this month, driving US Treasury yields higher and putting pressure on equity valuations.

Government bond selling moderated later in the session, with analysts suggesting that some investors were moving away from riskier AI-related equities and towards US government debt.

Concerns have also increased about the sustainability of large-scale borrowing used to finance artificial intelligence infrastructure, particularly as financing costs remain elevated and competition within the sector intensifies.

CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), a cloud infrastructure company with significant exposure to AI computing demand, was among the hardest hit.

Its shares declined more than 15%, while some of the company's bonds fell to new lows in secondary market trading.

The movements highlighted growing investor attention to the financial risks associated with debt-funded expansion across the AI industry.

Anthropic Reports 45% Quarterly Revenue Growth, According to Media Reports

Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANTP) reportedly told institutional investors on Wednesday that its third-quarter revenue increased 45% to approximately $16.8 billion.

According to The Wall Street Journal, the developer of the Claude AI chatbot previously recorded revenue of $11.6 billion in the second quarter and less than $5 billion in the first quarter.

September's consumer price index climbed 0.6% from the previous month, while advancing 3.7% on an annual basis. Although monthly inflation matched forecasts, the yearly figure topped expectations, as analysts surveyed by Dow Jones had projected a 3.6% gain.

Stripping out volatile food and energy costs, core CPI rose 0.3% month-over-month and 2.6% year-over-year. These figures marginally outpaced Wall Street estimates, which called for increases of 0.2% and 2.5%, respectively.

Osaic Chief Market Strategist Philip Blancato told CNBC that the data keeps a December rate hike firmly on the table for the Federal Reserve, adding that elevated crude prices could keep core inflation near 3% next year.

Most of the inflation pressure came from elevated oil or energy prices, with prices for gasoline averaging at $4.33 a gallon, compared to about $3.08 per gallon a year earlier, according to AAA.
